headline_marked: NCP's Nahid Islam: [[Government has completely failed]] in first 180 days
headline: NCP's Nahid Islam: Government has completely failed in first 180 days
summary: The National Citizens Party (NCP) claims the administration is returning to a fascist structure due to inefficiency and a lack of planning.
details: Nahid Islam, the convener of the National Citizens Party (NCP) and opposition chief whip, stated that while six months is not enough for a full evaluation, the government has failed in its first 180 days.
During a press conference at the NCP's temporary central office in Banglamotor, Dhaka, the party highlighted several failures of the administration.

Islam criticized the government's handling of the energy crisis, load shedding, rising electricity prices, and the failure to address the 'ham' issue, while accusing them of shifting blame onto the interim government.
He further noted that the democratic environment is shrinking due to a lack of trust in the investigation of disappearances, an ineffective Human Rights Commission, and the harassment of journalists.
The NCP convener warned that if the government returns to 'old politics,' it will face massive public protests.
He also called for the effective implementation of the verdict against Sheikh Hasina and improving the relations between India and Bangladesh.
caption:
The National Citizens Party claims the government has failed in its first 180 days, warning of a return to fascist structures.

Nahid Islam, the convener of the National Citizens Party (NCP) and opposition chief whip, stated that while six months is not enough for a full evaluation, the government has failed in its first 180 days.

During a press conference at the NCP's temporary central office in Banglamotor, Dhaka, the party highlighted several failures of the administration.

Islam criticized the government's handling of the energy crisis, load shedding, rising electricity prices, and the failure to address the 'ham' issue, while accusing them of shifting blame onto the interim government.

He further noted that the democratic environment is shrinking due to a lack of trust in the investigation of disappearances, an ineffective Human Rights Commission, and the harassment of journalists.

The NCP convener warned that if the government returns to 'old politics,' it will face massive public protests.

He also called for the effective implementation of the verdict against Sheikh Hasina and improving the relations between India and Bangladesh.

headline_marked: Nusrat murder: [[HC upholds death penalty for 2]], acquits 10
headline: Nusrat murder: HC upholds death penalty for 2, acquits 10
summary: The High Court has confirmed the death sentences for two convicts in the 2019 Nusrat Jahan murder case, while commuting four others to life imprisonment.
details: The High Court has upheld the death penalty for Siraj Ud-Daula, the dismissed principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil Madrasa, and Shahadat Hossain Shamim in the Nusrat Jahan murder case.
Additionally, the court commuted the sentences of four other convicts to life imprisonment and acquitted 10 others.
Nusrat Jahan, a student at the madrasa, was set on fire on April 6, 2019, on the roof of a cyclone shelter while she was attending her Alim examinations.
After the attack, she was treated at Sonagazi Upazila Health Complex, Feni General Hospital, and later the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Nusrat passed away on April 10, 2019, while undergoing treatment.
A case was filed by her brother, Mahmudul Hasan, and the charge sheet was submitted on May 28, 2019.
In October 2019, a lower court had sentenced 16 people to death. The High Court's ruling today follows the review of death references and appeals filed by the convicts.
caption:
Two men face the death penalty after the High Court upheld their sentences for the brutal murder of madrasa student Nusrat Jahan.

The High Court has upheld the death penalty for Siraj Ud-Daula, the dismissed principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil Madrasa, and Shahadat Hossain Shamim in the Nusrat Jahan murder case.

Additionally, the court commuted the sentences of four other convicts to life imprisonment and acquitted 10 others.

Nusrat Jahan, a student at the madrasa, was set on fire on April 6, 2019, on the roof of a cyclone shelter while she was attending her Alim examinations.

After the attack, she was treated at Sonagazi Upazila Health Complex, Feni General Hospital, and later the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Nusrat passed away on April 10, 2019, while undergoing treatment.

A case was filed by her brother, Mahmudul Hasan, and the charge sheet was submitted on May 28, 2019.

In October 2019, a lower court had sentenced 16 people to death. The High Court's ruling today follows the review of death references and appeals filed by the convicts.
